payload.claim: The only range-boundary check is the upper bound (`cite.end > len(lines)`); there is no check that `cite.start >= 1` or that `cite.start <= cite.end`. A citation like `path:0` or a reversed range like `path:20-5` parses successfully (the regex at line 1772 only requires digits) and, when the sentence has no other backticked text so `cite.candidates` is empty, `_moved_lines` (line 1851) returns `[]` immediately at line 1856, so no defect is ever printed for it — the malformed citation is silently reported as fully resolved. For a citation with candidates, the same inputs make `lines[cite.start - 1 : cite.end]` at line 1857 slice with a negative or inverted range, producing a nonsensical (usually empty) `ranged` rather than any indication the citation itself is malformed.
